summary: Root cause is the order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) at 07:40, which renamed the OrderExecuted field qty -> quantity and set the event header to schema v2. settlement-service still deserializes with the v1 schema expecting 'qty', so the first v2 event (orders-3@8841207) fails to deserialize at 07:42:14, becomes a poison message, and repeatedly blocks partition orders-3, halting settlements and driving consumer_lag from ~48 to 60k+. The reported config change cfg-3004 (poll records 500->200 at 07:35) is a red herring: no errors or lag rise occurred in the 7 minutes after it applied, and it cannot explain a schema-deserialization failure. CPU rose to ~70% from the retry loop but DB pool stayed flat ~6, ruling out DB/resource exhaustion. The main fix is a rollback/canary of order-service dep-6010 (or a settlement-side v2 schema/backward-compatible consumer), not touching the poll config.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 event schema change breaks settlement deserialization
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty -> quantity and bumped the schema header to v2, but settlement-service still deserializes with the v1 schema expecting 'qty'. The renamed event (orders-3@8841207) fails to deserialize, becomes a poison message, and repeatedly blocks partition orders-3, so settlement-service stops posting settlements from that partition and consumer lag grows unbounded.

causal_chain.claim: order-service dep-6010 at 07:40 renames qty->quantity and sets event header v2
settlement-service consumer still uses v1 schema expecting 'qty' and fails to deserialize the first v2 event at 07:42:14
the un-deserializable message becomes a poison message that blocks partition orders-3 (retried tens of thousands of times)
partition 3 stays blocked, no settlements posted, consumer_lag climbs from ~48 to 60k+
retry-loop spinning raises CPU to ~70% while DB pool stays flat, ruling out DB saturation

assumptions: The renamed 'quantity' field is not also emitted under a 'qty' alias, so v1 consumers cannot read it
orders-3 is the partition carrying the affected event stream and the blocked partition is a real availability impact, not an isolated bad record

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change cfg-3004 (poll batch size) caused the stall
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Lowering consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 on settlement-service at 07:35 reduced throughput enough to stall the consumer and grow lag.

causal_chain.claim: lag would start rising immediately after 07:35

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No errors or lag rise in the 7 minutes after cfg-3004 applied; the first deserialize error (07:42:14) and the lag spike (07:40 bucket) follow the order-service deploy at 07:40, not the config change. A smaller poll batch alone cannot produce a schema-deserialization poison message.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka partition reassignment / broker issue (per HIST-112 pattern)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A Kafka broker rebalance or partition reassignment caused settlement-service to lose its assignment and stall.

causal_chain.claim: partition reassignment causes lag and stuck settlements

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Logs show a specific deserialization failure and poison-message retry on offset orders-3@8841207 tied to an event schema/field rename, which partition reassignment would not produce. The historical match is a symptom-level lead only.

facts.statement: settlement-service consumer_lag exploded from ~48 (07:30 bucket) to 1572 (07:40) to 60k+ (09:50), starting exactly at the order-service deploy time.
settlement-service error stream shows a v1-vs-v2 schema mismatch: "missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)", first at 07:42:14.
The un-deserializable offset orders-3@8841207 is retried as a poison message, blocking partition orders-3.
order-service dep-6010 v2.16.0 renamed OrderExecuted qty -> quantity and bumped the schema header to v2 at 07:40.
The config change cfg-3004 (poll records 500->200 at 07:35) preceded no errors and no lag rise, and does not explain a deserialization failure.
settlement-service CPU rose to ~70% from the retry loop while db_pool_in_use stayed flat ~6 and pool was reported healthy.
HTTP error_rate on settlement-service stayed flat ~0.2%, so the impact is consumer-side, not request-serving.

assumptions: The renamed 'quantity' field has no 'qty' alias, so v1 consumers cannot read v2 events.
The recurring orders-3@8841207 poison message is representative of the blocking condition (a real bad record), not merely a noisy retry counter.
order-service is the sole producer of OrderExecuted events consumed by settlement-service.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-3004 applied on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 (log confirms at 07:35:37)
order-service deploys dep-6010 v2.16.0 (OrderExecuted qty->quantity, schema header v2); rollout completes 07:40:01
settlement-service consumer_lag jumps from ~48 to avg 1572 in this bucket
First deserialization error: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)
First poison-message line: orders-3@8841207 retried, partition blocked
Incident reported (settlements stuck ~40 min, lag 60k and climbing)
consumer_lag reaches avg 59267.74 / max 61605.53; errors still ongoing

recommended_actions.action: Roll back or pause order-service dep-6010 v2.16.0 (or re-emit OrderExecuted with a backward-compatible 'qty' alias / keep schema v1) to stop producing v2 events the consumer cannot read
recommended_actions.rationale: The schema change is the identified trigger; stopping v2 events removes the poison-message source so partition orders-3 can drain.

recommended_actions.action: After the producer is fixed, skip/dead-letter the stuck offset orders-3@8841207 so partition 3 unblocks and the consumer catches up
recommended_actions.rationale: A single poison message is blocking the whole partition; it must be skipped or DLQ'd to restore posting.

recommended_actions.action: Add a schema-registry compatibility gate (backward-compatible evolution, e.g. additive fields) so producers cannot emit a schema version consumers lack
recommended_actions.rationale: A rename + header bump was shipped without consumer readiness, breaking a live consumer.

recommended_actions.action: Make the consumer forward-tolerant: honor the event schema header and/or dead-letter un-deserializable records instead of blocking the partition indefinitely
recommended_actions.rationale: Poison-message handling turned one bad record into a full partition stall.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT revert cfg-3004 as the primary fix; if desired, re-evaluate the poll batch size separately after recovery
recommended_actions.rationale: The config change is not the cause; reverting it would not restore service and could confuse the fix.

data_gaps: No order-service producer-side log confirming the exact payload/schema of offset orders-3@8841207 was retrieved; the qty->quantity mapping is inferred from the deploy change summary plus the consumer error text.
No Kafka broker/partition telemetry was queried, so an independent broker-side contribution (e.g. rebalance) cannot be fully excluded — though logs point clearly to a schema failure.
Consumer_lag metric is aggregate; per-partition lag was not directly retrieved, so the claim that only orders-3 is affected rests on the uniform orders-3@8841207 error reference.

findings.statement: settlement-service consumer_lag was flat at ~40-65 messages from 06:00 through the 07:30 bucket (avg 47.78), then jumped to avg 1572.1 (max 3512) in the 07:40 bucket and grew monotonically to avg 59267.74 (max 61605.53) by 09:50.

settlement-service first ERROR is at 07:42:14: "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)". This exact pattern is the top error (213 occurrences) and persists through 09:58.

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)

findings.statement: settlement-service logs a poison message on the same offset repeatedly: "poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt ...), partition blocked" (196 occurrences, first_seen 07:44:51), with attempt counters in the tens of thousands.

refs.quote: poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked
poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 61790), partition blocked

findings.statement: order-service deployed dep-6010 v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z with summary "Order events v2" and changes: "OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity", "add field venue", "event schema version header v2". Status live, not rolled back.

refs.quote: OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity

findings.statement: order-service logged "deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready" at 2026-05-12T07:40:01Z, immediately before settlement errors began.

refs.quote: deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready

findings.statement: Config change cfg-3004 on settlement-service changed consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z (applied per log at 07:35:37). This is the only config change in the window.
No ERROR-level entries appear between the cfg-3004 application (07:35:37) and 07:42:14; the two logs in that gap are INFO "scheduled job heartbeat ok".
settlement-service CPU jumped from ~27.5% (07:30 bucket) to ~60.8% (07:40) and held ~70% thereafter, while db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~6 connections for the entire window.
settlement-service consumer_lag rise is confined to partition orders-3 (all errors reference orders-3@8841207), and HTTP error_rate for settlement-service stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout.

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)

findings.statement: settlement-service logs show healthy DB pool ("connection pool stats: healthy") and successful scheduled-job heartbeats throughout, with no restart or crash lines.

Historical post-mortem HIST-112 (settlement-service, 2026-02-03) described the same lag/settlements-stuck symptom but attributed it to partition reassignment during broker maintenance — a different root cause than the current schema mismatch.

refs.quote: Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment
